question: Fusion of light nuclei releases energy in stars, but controlled thermonuclear fusion is difficult to achieve on Earth. Give two physics-based reasons for this difficulty.

options.A: Controlled fusion is difficult only because fusion reactions release too little energy.
options.B: Fusion requires low temperature so that nuclei can remain close together in a solid container.
options.C: Positively charged light nuclei strongly repel each other, so extremely high temperature is needed to bring them within nuclear range. The resulting hot plasma is very difficult to confine for sufficient time without touching material walls.
options.D: Fusion is difficult because neutrons must always be slowed down by a moderator before they can fuse.
